subject: AP: urgent — BlueFjord production throttling due to quota/burst policy
messages:
From: Lena Sørensen <lena@bluefjord.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:15:23 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden 429s + latency spike — urgent

Jordan —

We started seeing widespread 429 responses and 3–4x latency on our inference endpoints around 07:48 UTC. Traffic pattern didn’t change on our side — the rate was within our committed throughput. A non-negligible portion of requests are failing intermittently which is affecting live features (session timeouts for customers).

Examples: request IDs 34f2a5 / 34f2a8 / 34f2b1 include repeated 429 with X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0 then spike back. Attached is an excerpt of the client-side retry logs and a screenshot of our SLO dashboard showing errors rising since the window flip at 07:45.

This is P1 for us — can you confirm whether this is a config change on your side (burst/quota/pacing) or a transient capacity issue? We need immediate mitigation or a rollback.

- Lena
Lena Sørensen
Head of Integrations, BlueFjord Analytics
lena@bluefjord.ai

Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden 429s + latency spike — urgent

Forwarding BlueFjord P1 — they report immediate 429s + high latencies; they are in eu-west and hitting our hosted endpoints (confirmed in logs). Highlights from their logs: sustained short bursts that should have fit their reserved pacing, several requests show X-Burst-Window-Exceeded and X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0.

Ask: can SRE validate whether a policy change was rolled (token-bucket/burst-window) or whether a safety valve (global burst cap) triggered? If capacity constrained, can we: 1) temporarily relax burst window for BF account, 2) add fallback to the compatible model variant, or 3) route to Dedicated pool if available? This is impacting live customers — needs priority.

Attached: bf_request_logs.txt, SLO screenshot (from customer). I’ve opened JIRA-INF-4921.

— Jordan
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:34 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden 429s + latency spike — urgent

Got it — looking now. Quick summary after initial checks:
- No recent code rollout to the rate limiter in the last 72h.
- We did flip a global safety cap on burst windows for eu-west at 07:44 to contain cross-tenant spikes (automated policy during a separate incident). It looks like BlueFjord’s sustained short bursts exceeded the tightened global burst allowance and hit per-account throttles.
- There is capacity in the Dedicated pool in eu-west but BlueFjord is on hosted tier.

Immediate mitigations I can do now:
1) Temporarily whitelist BlueFjord’s account to the previous burst window profile for 2 hours (low risk) — will remove after incident.
2) Provision routing to eu-west dedicated nodes for the next 24h while we monitor (requires authorization).
3) Enable fallback to smaller model variant to reduce per-request cost if they accept slight quality tradeoff.

Recommend 1) immediately and 2) if we need sustained headroom. I will enact 1) in 5 minutes unless someone objects. Also recommend CS coordinate messaging and crediting policy with Marissa.

— Vivek
VP, SRE
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:14:52 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden 429s + latency spike — urgent

Thanks for the quick triage. Authorize the temporary whitelist of the previous burst profile for 24h to give BlueFjord breathing room — extend if metrics haven’t normalized. Also approve routing to Dedicated nodes for 24h as a precaution; we’ll treat this as an operational uplift, not automatic migration.

On credits: approve a goodwill credit equivalent to 1 week of usage for the impacted SLA period. CS (Monica/Hannah) to draft the note and include a concrete MAP (mutual_action_plan.docx) that outlines steps and timelines.

Keep me posted if the dedicated pool looks saturated or if other accounts are affected by the safety cap flip.

— Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lena Sørensen <lena@bluefjord.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:42:09 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + latency spike — urgent

Lena —

Quick update: we identified that a global safety cap on burst windows in eu-west was tightened at 07:44 and that change interacted poorly with BlueFjord’s short sustained bursts. We have:
- Temporarily restored BlueFjord’s previous burst window profile (effective now).
- Provisioned routing to dedicated nodes in eu-west for the next 24 hours.
- Enabled optional fallback to the compatible smaller model if you want to reduce token cost/latency immediately (let us know).

Marissa approved a one-week goodwill credit; Monica/Hannah will send the formal note and MAP which includes a staged rollout and an optimization plan (batching + KV caching) to avoid repeat. We’ve attached the incident logs for your review and opened JIRA-INF-4921 for post-mortem.

Please confirm if latency is back to acceptable levels on your side and whether you want us to enable fallback. Apologies again — we’ll follow with a detailed RCA once the post-mortem completes.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
